rounds.text: Rachit Prints Ltd presents a compelling value case underpinned by elite capital efficiency and robust top-line momentum, trading at a modest P/E of 15.6x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 6.71x below the sector benchmark of 9x [E11]. The business generates superior returns, highlighted by a robust ROCE of 20.79% against a sector benchmark of 8.39% [E10] and a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E20], supported by strong operational scaling where compounded sales growth reached 18% over three years [E14] and 20% in the trailing twelve months [E15]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by 5 percentage points to 17% in the TTM compared to three years prior [E22], while a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of Rs 427 per share suggests a significant margin of safety of 61.6% over the current market price of Rs 164 [E34, E35]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -3.60 Cr in March 2026 with a weak cash conversion of -0.79x [E26, E27], and the company currently pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

Despite reported profits, Rachit Prints Ltd exhibits severe cash generation failures, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.60 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -12.70 Cr for March 2026, leading to a distressed cash conversion ratio of -0.79x [E26, E28]. Operational efficiency is rapidly deteriorating as working capital days have ballooned from 72.6 days to 133 days, while borrowings have simultaneously increased to Rs 12.66 Cr in September 2026 [E30, E43]. Furthermore, the company carries specific financial risks with explicit flags indicating it is not paying out dividends despite reported profits, and that it might be capitalizing interest costs [E41, E42]. Operating margins show instability, reading as inconsistent over both the last two years and the last two quarters [E24, E25]. Expectations may also be running ahead of delivery since recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 14% [E38]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales and profit growth alongside robust headline returns on capital, such as an ROE of 19.4% and an ROCE of 20.79% [E9, E10, E15, E17].

Conceded: the company posted a negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.60 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -12.70 Cr for March 2026 [E26, E28]. However, this cash burn occurs against a backdrop of powerful top-line expansion, with 3-year compounded sales growth at 18% and TTM sales growth accelerating to 20% [E14, E15]. While the bear highlights ballooning working capital days [E43], the business easily outpaces sector benchmarks with an ROE of 19.4% against 7.19% and an ROCE of 20.79% against 8.39% [E9, E10]. Conceded: the company does not pay out a dividend despite reported profits [E41], but capital is being productively retained to generate a 5-year median ROE of 27% and a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E19, E20]. Conceded: operating margins are flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25], yet the TTM operating margin actually expanded by 5 percentage points to 17% compared to three years earlier [E22]. Finally, the reverse DCF proves the market is pricing in a mere 4.8% growth rate, vastly underappreciating a company whose base case and recent performance run at vastly higher levels [E36, E45, E47].

Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 18% and TTM sales growth is 20% [E14, E15]. However, the bull's dismissal of the cash burn ignores that operating cash flow collapsed to Rs -3.60 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -12.70 Cr in March 2026, creating a severe cash conversion ratio of -0.79x against reported profits [E26, E28]. Conceded: the company demonstrates high reported returns such as a 19.4% ROE and 20.79% ROCE [E9, E10], but these accounting gains are severely undermined by a massive ballooning in working capital days from 72.6 days to 133 days alongside a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E42, E43]. Conceded: the TTM operating margin expanded to 17% [E22], yet the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are officially flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25]. Furthermore, borrowings have climbed to Rs 12.66 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 10.89 Cr a year earlier [E30], while the company refuses to pay any dividend despite reporting profits [E41]. Finally, price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 14%, showing that expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery rather than being underappreciated by the market [E38].
